newsitem.title: USA: Justice warns lawyers against self-interest lobbying.
newsitem.headline: Justice warns lawyers against self-interest lobbying.

text.p: A Supreme Court Justice believes lawyers should shun self-interested lobbying and said that while they can be a "hired gun" for clients, they need not be one for themselves.

Justice Anthony Kennedy, who spoke Saturday night at the American Bar Association's annual meeting here, also said that individuals should be held responsible for their actions despite past injustices or persisting social ills.
Kennedy gave the keynote address at the group's opening assembly at which time Justice Sandra Day O'Connor received the ABA Medal, the association's highest honour.

"Few spectacles are more destructive of our professional standing than for a lawyer, or group of lawyers, to take a position on proposals to change the law based simply on the lawyer's own financial interests," Kennedy said.
"The profession and the nation deserve your detached judgment, not your self-interested lobbying. You sometimes must be a hired gun for someone else; you need not be a hired gun for yourself."
On another topic, Kennedy told lawyers they must insist on the responsibility of the individual.
"Our society is a compassionate one and so it is tempted to excuse the individual from responsibility because of past injustice or persisting social ills," he said.
"A concern with these deficiencies is necessary if we are to improve our society, but this concern ought not to be carried so far that the idea of personal, moral responsibility is eroded."

Kennedy cited as an example the use of diminished capacity as a defence to a crime. He told of a case of a man who was prosecuted for a crime committed while he was participating in a riot. The man's defence was diminished capacity because he was caught up in the excitement and emotion of events.
"This is a strange twist of the rule of law," Kennedy said.

"When our nation accounts to history, we will not have the defence of diminished capacity. And when our heroes are counted, they will be ones who recognised that individual responsibility is a celebration of freedom, not its denial."
